title: Performative Prediction
authors: Juan C. Perdomo, Tijana Zrnic, Celestine Mendler-Dünner, and Moritz Hardt
corrected_formalization_scope: The completed corrected target uses a compact-convex domain and explicit decoupled-risk continuity in Proposition 4.1, adds |mu| <= 1/2 to the Proposition 4.2 witness, requires gamma <= beta in Proposition 3.6(c), and proves Theorem 3.10 through dimension > 2 concrete RERM/RGD concentration schedules with explicit bounded-moment, measurability, loss/integrability, numerical-budget, and entry premises.
infinite_adaptive_trace_scope: The reusable `adaptiveFreshHeterogeneousInfiniteTraceLaw` now constructs one dependent-coordinate Ionescu--Tulcea probability law for all adaptive finite-PMF batches (dummy coordinate 0, then round t at coordinate t+1). Its history-conditional event theorem and the full inverse-square union bound yield literal all-rounds <= p results for PZ's RERM uniform-loss, RGD empirical-gradient-mass, and finite-alphabet primal-W1 events, and the finite-PMF schedule constructors instantiate all three. Measurable event cylinders plus the reusable prefix-complement bridge lift the finite-alphabet W1 complement to an all-rounds RGD absorbing-ball theorem. This does not identify the older fixed-horizon PMF types by marginal equality, nor does it prove the source's general empirical-Wasserstein/Fournier--Guillin theorem or its exact constants.
infinite_adaptive_trace_upstream: Mathlib Ionescu--Tulcea trajectory implementation reused directly: https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/IonescuTulcea/Traj.html and https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/IonescuTulcea/Traj.lean.
finite_wasserstein_concentration_scope: An explicit maximal finite coupling proves W₁(empirical, law) ≤ diameter * card(Data) * epsilon from coordinatewise empirical mass deviations. The corresponding finite-IID W₁ failure event is bounded by the existing mass-deviation event and its Hoeffding bound; the heterogeneous conditionally-IID Ionescu--Tulcea trace lifts that literal event to a countable-union inverse-square confidence bound. A selected positive finite batch schedule meets that bound for the literal W₁ event itself, uniformly over every history-dependent deployment rule. Measurable round cylinders and the direct no-W₁-bad-trace recurrence then give the RGD absorbing ball at every iteration with probability at least 1-p. This is a genuine primal-W₁ finite-alphabet specialization, not the source's Fournier--Guillin theorem or its constants/rate.
hilbert_projection_scope: The reusable `hilbertProjection` selects the nearest point on every nonempty closed convex subset of a complete real inner-product space, proves the variational characterization required by projected-gradient fixed-point arguments, and proves 1-Lipschitzness. It directly reuses Mathlib's Hilbert projection theorem: https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/Minimal.html and https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/master/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Projection/Minimal.lean. Theorem 3.8's arbitrary-law A1/A2 endpoint instantiates it; this does not discharge the theorem's separate analytic or empirical-concentration boundaries.
latest_verified_progress: The general measure layer formalizes Theorems 3.5(a)--(b) and 3.8(a)--(b) on a nonempty closed convex parameter domain, including arbitrary-law W1 sensitivity, frozen-risk interpolation, Appendix E.3's T2/T3 estimates, the projected-RGD Banach fixed point, and its geometric rate. The selected Euclidean projection is now constructed extensionally by direct reuse of Mathlib's Hilbert projection theorem and instantiated in the A1/A2 Theorem 3.8 endpoint. The reusable Mathlib-backed dominated parametric-integral bridge derives frozen-risk gradients from A1 together with explicit local loss measurability, integrable domination, and pointwise differentiability. That same bridge now supplies arbitrary-law W1 endpoints for Theorem 4.3's `2 Lz epsilon / gamma` distance bound and Corollary 5.1's `2 Lz epsilon (Ltheta + Lz epsilon) / gamma` objective gap. Proposition 3.6(a) now formalizes the source's arbitrary-positive-epsilon/beta real linear-loss/Dirac model, its exact decoupled risk and domain RRM update, W1 sensitivity via reusable Dirac transport, actual gradient, convexity, beta-joint smoothness, absence of positive strong convexity, unique stable point, and nonconvergent selected endpoint trajectory. Proposition 3.6(b) now formalizes its real regularized-hinge/Dirac model, exact frozen risk, W1 sensitivity, pointwise gamma-strong convexity, and hinge nondifferentiability, with the two source RRM steps certified on their divergent orbit. Proposition 3.6(c) now formalizes the source's real squared-loss/Dirac model, its exact decoupled risk and RRM update, W1 sensitivity via a reusable Dirac coupling, A1/A2 constants, fixed-point characterization, and the stated no-stability/divergence regimes. Proposition 4.1 has an arbitrary-law compact-convex best-response/Kakutani endpoint under explicit joint-risk continuity and pointwise loss convexity; a finite compact nonconvex counterexample proves that the source's compact-only statement needs this convex-domain correction. The general-law empirical interface realizes a nonempty finite sample as a probability measure and proves the deterministic W1 event-to-gradient/update step of Theorem 3.10. General empirical-Wasserstein concentration and the source Wasserstein/Berge continuity bridge remain open.
human_summary: The shared game-theory library now formalizes finite performative risk, decoupled risk, stability, selected repeated-risk minimization over a domain, finite argmin existence, strategic induced laws, finite transport-coupling and finite-W₁ Lipschitz-test bounds, frozen-risk strong convexity, finite expected-loss differentiation, source-shaped primal and finite-W₁ convex-domain RRM and projected-RGD contraction/geometric-convergence theorems, finite-W₁ versions of Theorem 4.3 and Corollary 5.1, the finite-PMF compact-convex Proposition 4.1 route, and finite-IID support plus finite-horizon deterministic/union-bound bridges for Theorem 3.10. The arbitrary-measure Theorems 3.5 and 3.8 now match their W₁ contraction and Banach conclusions under explicit finite-first-moment coupling, integrability, and local analytic-differentiation premises. The source's Euclidean projection is constructed extensionally for the arbitrary-law Theorem 3.8 route by direct reuse of Mathlib's Hilbert projection theorem. Proposition 3.6(a) is now an exact real linear-loss/Dirac counterexample for all positive epsilon and beta: its decoupled risk, domain RRM update, W₁ sensitivity, actual gradient, convexity, beta-joint smoothness, lack of strong convexity, unique stable point, and selected nonconvergent cycle are compiled; its interface also retains the source proposition’s otherwise vacuous positive gamma quantifier. Proposition 3.6(b) is now an exact real regularized-hinge/Dirac counterexample: its frozen risk, W₁ sensitivity, pointwise gamma-strong convexity, hinge nondifferentiability, and the two domain-constrained RRM steps on the divergent orbit are compiled. Proposition 3.6(c) is likewise an exact real squared-loss/Dirac counterexample: its decoupled risk, RRM update, W₁ sensitivity, A1/A2 constants, stability fixed point, and the source’s equality/no-stability and divergence regimes are compiled. Proposition 4.1 derives compact nonempty and convex frozen-law argmin values plus a closed graph from a visible joint-risk-continuity bridge, then applies a source-attributed local Kakutani port; the printed compact-only statement is false, as a compiled compact nonconvex counterexample shows, and the source's arbitrary-distribution Wasserstein/Berge bridge remains open. Theorem 3.10 includes recursively defined deployed-state PMFs, including a heterogeneous batch-history law that uses a separate `n_t` at each round, with conditional IID event factorization and an exact finite-prefix inverse-square confidence bridge for both its RERM uniform-loss and RGD empirical-mass events. In the finite-PMF model, vanishing parameter-uniform failures now construct positive roundwise batch counts satisfying that bridge, whose no-bad-event consequences give the corresponding RERM/RGD absorbing-ball conclusion with probability at least `1-p` for every fixed horizon. A reused finite-family Hoeffding result gives a direct RERM budget condition when losses are `[0,1]`; neither finite route reproduces the source's quantitative Fournier--Guillin bound. Fournier--Guillin's official and arXiv sources are pinned; their theorem’s dimension/tail-dependent concentration assumptions and constants remain separate formal work. The library also constructs a corrected finite-PMF form of Proposition 4.2's Bernoulli example, checks its exact quadratic risk, concavity algebra, full loss-side joint-smoothness/strong-convexity calculation, and finite W₁ sensitivity by an explicit coupling, while identifying the source appendix's missing endpoint condition. The source paper's general Wasserstein concentration, exact empirical-Wasserstein/source-constant bridge, and arbitrary-distribution/primal-dual bridge are not yet formalized.

human_summary_review.note: Set to human_approved only after a human has written or explicitly approved this summary; do not rewrite a human_approved summary without explicit human instruction.

human_review.source: v11 PaperInterface claim surface; human entries are recorded after direct review

llm_statement_review.policy: For every selected source claim, compare only its exact byte-pinned raw source-anchor bundle and Lean's expanded transparent `...Spec : Prop` target. The paired proof endpoint receives separate Lean-Meta proof credit; a name, paraphrase, wrapper, or prior aggregate receipt is not a semantic match. Review every retained paper-local prerequisite and every material library prerequisite before the dependent claim.

llm_paper_coverage_review.policy: Maintain an audit/paper_statement_map.json inventory of source definitions, formulas, and named statements, then use a separate LLM pass to judge whether each source item is covered by one or more dashboard rows. If coverage uses a reusable library declaration, it must route through an audited paper-local semantic bridge/equivalence row; matching by Lean/library/source names is not semantic evidence. Quarantined source defects require a separate exact-hash semantic judgment binding each candidate counterexample/refutation theorem to the validated defect record and every elaborated signature atom. This paper-level accounting is required before calling a full-paper formalization closed and is separate from row-local statement matching.

llm_assumption_review.policy: Every paper-facing theorem premise not derived from prior Lean declarations must be declared in Assumptions.lean, listed in assumption_names, and judged by an independent LLM as a true paper/source model assumption rather than a proof assumption.

llm_source_record_review.policy: Run the code-backed recursive source-record audit for any visible record, certificate, replay, process, bridge, source-row, or broad package premise. The LLM judge must classify each boundary-shaped input and recursive field by source evidence, Lean derivation, approved external boundary, or unresolved proof debt.

semantic_model_review.policy: For every reviewed row, preserve an alpha-normalized expanded binder/domain surface, including transparent local type aliases, record parameter domains, and model records reached only in result quantifiers. An unexpanded local opaque/constant type requires a checked carrier/refinement bridge rather than being silently treated as an ordinary carrier. When an expanded finite carrier uses index arithmetic such as Fin (n + c), record the source cardinal parameter, the expanded Lean expression, and a proved parameter translation; then explicitly compare it with pinned source text. Review endpoint support/cutoffs, product or iid laws versus source state evolution, conditioning/calibration semantics, expectation definedness, null-cell totalization and finite/countable/arbitrary partition scope, and Real versus extended-rate codomains when the expanded model makes them relevant. For a probability-law surface, state whether conditioning is pointwise, a.e., positive-fiber, or event-calibrated; state measurability/integrability or extended-value conventions for every expectation; and expose every zero-mass-cell branch. Local declaration and binder names are routing only; detected probability/rate shapes need a checked bridge from source primitives. Because this scaffold enables explicit v10 source routes, every full closeout requires current source-record semantic-model judgments for every generated row; an unresolved model dimension blocks both full statuses.

source_proof_fidelity_review.policy: Audit source proof steps by source locator and mathematical claim, not by Lean declaration name. Completed papers use ledger schema 2. Every defect records status_impact as formalized_note, formalized_with_caveat, or partially_formalized plus a semantic rationale. Minor repairs with an unchanged substantive endpoint are notes; formalized with caveat is reserved for a substantial central source-paper error with a fully proved corrected endpoint; weaker Lean targets and added non-source assumptions are partial. Keep this configured ledger whenever explicit source routes or source-defect links are present; a formalized note cannot waive an added non-source assumption or a partial boundary.
